reviewMethod: All 19 selected stored body images across five current-corpus Organic Letters papers were independently rehashed against the immutable read-only GitHub evidence artifact and checked for exact task/page/article/source DOI identity, original Figure/Scheme identity and independent caption, captureVersion/job identity, fixed media generation 1790082000000, content-addressed R2 key, actual byte length/type/dimensions, duplicate source/hash ownership, frozen deployed same-ID body state and TOC separation. SVG files were parsed/rendered and checked for active/external content; PNG files were decoded and dimension-checked. Every image was visually reviewed against its owning caption and article theme for body-image role, unrelated/recommendation contamination, duplicate risk and legibility. Capture success/partial/controller/transport checkpoints were treated only as provenance evidence, not semantic approval. No publisher request, R2/D1 write, direct import/repair, literature/card/title/scope mutation, userscript change or media-generation change was performed.
quality: All 19 selected files matched their full SHA256, byte lengths, dimensions, content-hash prefixes and strict content-addressed R2 key formula. No selected full hash, source URL or R2 key had a cross-DOI ownership collision in the frozen evidence inventory. The successful 18:00 GitHub Pages deployment artifact retained distinct official TOCs and contained no deployed body figures or publication-ledger records for these five papers before this review. Partial article reports are handled per-image only; missing figures are not inferred, and controller/transport checkpoints are not assigned to VPN, R2, quota or publisher causes. Figure 1 assets remain body-only and are not TOC substitutions.
